text: and then a life, yours. It does not arrive all at once. It comes in flashes. The way memory actually
works. A hospital ceiling, too bright. A hand, impossibly large, closing around your whole fist.
The smell of rain on hot pavement. The birth they handle going out. The particular silence of a
house where someone has just stopped loving someone. You grew. You learned the rules of the heavy
world. How to want, how to hide, how to perform being a person. You were good at it. The way a
native speaker is good at a language. Nobody suspected you were translating from a tongue with no
word for a loan. There were moments weren't there? When the translation failed, a sunset that hurt,
a song in a language you never learned that made you weep. Standing in a crowd surrounded,
celebrated, and feeling like the only awake person in a city of sleepwalkers. You called it melancholy.
The doctors had other names. It was none of those things. It was the stone in deep water,
shifting. It was the part of you that is still awake, turning over in its sleep.
